trust_decision.summary: Whether a diagram-supplied id may be any word (including `__proto__`/`constructor`) and be stored and looked up as a plain object key, or must be rejected; decided in the architecture diagram's id stores and existence checks in architectureDb.ts, mirrored by the group-keyed alignment maps in architectureRenderer.ts.

landing_point.why: These are the only nested plain-object writes keyed by diagram ids in the diagram: when a node's `in` is `__proto__`, `groupAlignments['__proto__'] ??= {}` is a no-op (Object.prototype is truthy) and the next line writes onto Object.prototype.

mermaid.parse()/mermaid.render() -> architectureParser.populateDb service statements (`service a(...) in __proto__`)
mermaid.parse() -> populateDb junction statements (`junction mid in <parent>`)

fix_sites.entry_point: compile-time types shared by the DB and renderer, plus the new architectureGroupAlignmentKey helper used at both sites

O3_reason_to_dismiss: It is a different layer (layout, not the DB), it only reads the alignment result, and its own group-keyed buckets (`horizontalAlignments[y][nodeGroup]`) throw a TypeError instead of polluting - so a solver can argue the pollution report never needed to touch the renderer.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A diagram may legitimately declare `group __proto__(cloud)[Marker]` and place services in it: `__proto__` and other Object.prototype names must stay ordinary, usable ids (the fix's own test asserts the group is listed by db.getGroups()), so a deny-list / 'reject proto ids' fix breaks valid diagrams.

O6_input_shapes: `__proto__` as a declared service/junction/group id (must be accepted as a normal name)
`__proto__` (or another inherited Object.prototype name such as `constructor`) as a parent value in `service a(...) in <parent>` where no such group was declared
the same bypass on the three separate add* methods (addService, addJunction, addGroup) and on addEdge's endpoint existence checks
ids on both sides of an edge: the alignment write is symmetric, so either lhsGroupId or rhsGroupId can be the hostile name
numeric-string ids (`service 20`, `service 10`) whose order object key iteration reorders; insertion order must be preserved
`align row|column` members that are `__proto__`-named services/junctions (registeredIds lookup in addLayoutHint)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second id-keyed element store (e.g. per-group or per-edge DOM handles) written as `this.<store>[id] = element`.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The existing `elements[id]` pattern is copied straight from svgDraw's setElementForId(id, ...) calls with diagram ids; adding group or edge handles is a natural next step for a maintainer.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third group-id-keyed accumulator next to the horizontal/vertical alignment buckets (e.g. per-group node order for layout hints).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The layout code already needs group->nodes buckets and builds them with `map[group] ??= []` then `.push(id)`; a new axis or constraint bucket would be written the same way.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An extra id-keyed field on ArchitectureState (e.g. groupBoundingBoxes) alongside nodes/groups/registeredIds/elements.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The state type is a snapshot-ish Record<string, unknown> that already carries four id-keyed collections; a serializer/save-shaped store added here would be plausible and is not covered by the existing tests.

O9_family: prototype pollution (CWE-1321): diagram-controlled ids used as plain-object keys, writing onto Object.prototype from the group-alignment map

O10_build.language: TypeScript (plus a Langium grammar for the architecture parser)
O10_build.toolchain: pnpm 10 workspace; langium-cli generates the parser (.esbuild/build.ts:96 generateLangium); esbuild bundling; tsc for types; vitest 3 with jsdom (vite.config.ts:15-16)
O10_build.project_tests: packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/architecture/architecture.spec.ts (parser + DB unit tests, no rendering), svgDraw.spec.ts (jsdom render via jsdomIt), architectureSeed.spec.ts, and packages/parser/tests/architecture.test.ts for the grammar; rendering also covered only by Cypress e2e, which needs a browser.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Tighten the parent existence check to an own-key test (hasOwnProperty) so a bogus `__proto__` parent is rejected - the pollution goes away but `__proto__` still cannot be a declared group, so the hidden test that declares `group __proto__` still fails.

out_of_scope_notes: Other diagram types repeat the same id-as-key pattern and already have `__proto__`/`constructor` id tests (e.g. pie, sankey, state, er, class, flowchart, gantt, git, requirement, sequence); that is the sibling advisory's surface and was not pursued.
The init-directive config merge path (assignWithDepth/cleanAndMerge in packages/mermaid/src/utils.ts) is a separate, already deny-listed route via utils/sanitizeDirective.ts and was not audited.
unverified: Pinned repo size in MB could not be measured without a shell, so O4.repo_mb is null and tiny_repo/giant_repo were not flagged.

The published advisory text/report was not available here; I could not confirm whether it states that `__proto__` must remain a legal id and that numeric ids keep insertion order, although the fix's own tests require both (fix.diff:51-59 and fix.diff:76-84).

The TypeError claim for architectureRenderer.ts:223-229 when a node's parent is `__proto__` is reasoned from the code (Object.prototype has no push), not executed - running project code is out of bounds here.

Whether the benchmark's hidden tests assert the exact key format `"__proto__"-"myPrototypePollutionKey"` used by the fix (fix.diff:71-72, 733-736) is unknown; if they do, a secure Map-based fix with a different key format would fail for an implementation reason.
Latest release was given as none, so O8 present_in_latest is not applicable (O8 is empty).
